chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When the woman is pregnant, she is not stoned.

key_terms.تُرْجَمْ: She is stoned (passive verb from rajm)

ai.seo_question: Does pregnancy exempt a woman from the punishment of stoning in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this concise narration establishing that pregnancy serves as a legal impediment to the immediate execution of *rajm* (stoning) for an adulterous married woman. This ruling reflects the juristic principle of preserving the fetus, ensuring the punishment is deferred until after childbirth, a view supported by Shia scholars who prioritize the life of the unborn child within the context of hudud penalties.
